title: Synthetic heat pumps: defrost, mode, capacity, staging and the source loop (generated by CAMBER)
summary: SYNTHETIC, generated locally by CAMBER (no download, no real building): one small building's heat pumps through a fortnight of late winter with damp frosty days, a three-day cold snap, mild fog and a sunny spell, every 5 minutes. Four air-source units (zone and discharge-air temperatures, fan, occupancy, setpoints, compressor status and reversing valve): a healthy one, one whose defrost sensor reads far too cold, one on a 60-minute defrost timer and one whose strip heat has failed. Six water-source units (the same points with the compressor stage instead): two that share a room and agree, one with its reversing valve stuck in heating, one whose second stage hunts, and two that fight in one room. And the water-source units' loop (supply and return water, pump status, speed and DP): variable flow, and constant speed with the bypass stuck open.
teaches: excessive heat-pump defrost, a stuck reversing valve, a heat pump short of capacity in a cold snap, compressor stages that hunt and two units fighting in one room, which no open dataset shows
why a 15-minute trend cannot vouch for 5-minute defrosts and stage changes
a source loop that pumps water without carrying heat
choosing the reversals-per-day limit: a unit just under the default
publisher: CAMBER (generated locally by the user's copy)
citation: CAMBER synthetic dataset synthetic-heat-pump, generator heat_pump (camber.datasets._synthetic_heat_pump), seed 147. Generated data, not measurements from any building.
timezone: naive generated clock (no DST); 5-minute samples from 2025-02-17 (a Monday) for 14 days
equipment: 4 air-source heat pumps, 6 water-source heat pumps (two pairs sharing a room) and 2 source loops, as 12 scenarios

fault_types.excess_defrost: a defrost sensor reading far too cold: the unit defrosts every 30 minutes of heating at any outdoor temperature, frost or not
fault_types.capacity_shortfall: an air-source unit whose electric strip heat has failed: below its balance point the room falls out of its heating band
fault_types.wrong_mode: a water-source unit's reversing valve stuck in heating: every cooling call heats a room that is already too warm
fault_types.stage_hunting: a two-stage unit with a 0.1 F stage-2 differential and no stage-up delay: the second stage chatters on and off
fault_types.room_fight: two units in one room, one sensor by cold glass and one in the sun by the door: one heats while the other cools (hp_room_imbalance, a fleet rule, is not scored)
fault_types.flat_loop_deltat: a source loop at constant speed with the bypass stuck open: five times the design flow past the plant's sensors and almost no loop delta-T

full.description: all twelve scenarios (the same as default)

known_issues: Synthetic: generated by CAMBER's own model of a building and its heat pumps, not measured. It shows what the rules see, not how real heat pumps behave; never cite it as evidence about real buildings.

5-minute samples: a defrost or a stage change shorter than 5 minutes is invisible. Resampled to 15 minutes, a 5-minute defrost averages to a valve that reads heating, so the reversal and stage-change counts fall to a fraction (keep resample at 5min).
The water-source units' loop is modelled from the building's load, not from these six units' own compressors, and the units' capacity does not follow the loop temperature.
